alt: Three steps shared by every Paper 2 topic: factual content, then perspectives (functionalist, Marxist, feminist), then change and explanation. Below, Paper 1 builds the toolkit of methods and perspectives, and Paper 2 applies it; each paper is worth 50%.
caption: Facts, then perspectives, then change: the same route through Family, Education and Crime.

alt: Falling birth rates and rising life expectancy lead to an ageing population, which helps explain beanpole families, the sandwich generation and changing grandparent roles. Boomerang children belong instead to the changing roles of children. Below, the New Right see family diversity as dysfunction and postmodernists see it as choice.
caption: Connect each cause to its effects, and keep boomerang children in the right box.

alt: Three types of explanation for differences in achievement: material (such as access to digital technology), cultural (cultural capital and linguistic factors) and in-school (labelling and pro- and anti-school subcultures). Below, the hidden curriculum is applied to school uniform policies teaching conformity.
caption: Be ready to sort explanations into material, cultural and in-school.

alt: Two overlapping circles. Deviance is behaviour that breaks social norms; crime is behaviour that breaks the law. They overlap, but some deviance is not criminal, and both are relative across societies, cultures and time.
caption: Crime and deviance overlap but are not the same, and both are relative.

alt: Formal agencies of social control (police, courts, armed forces, government, penal system) beside informal agencies (family, education, workplace, peer group, media, religion), followed by the eleven named crime types, with organised/global, cyber, hate and domestic crime highlighted.
caption: Learn the control agencies as a paired list and classify crimes with the eleven types.

alt: A funnel narrowing from the true level of offending, to crime reported to the police, to crime recorded by the police, because of under-reporting by victims and under-recording by police; definitions also change over time. Below are the three measures named in the syllabus: official statistics, self-report studies and victim surveys.
caption: Under-reporting, under-recording and changing definitions separate recorded crime from the truth.

alt: Question 1 is always Family, Question 2 Education and Question 3 Crime, deviance and social control; each is worth 40 marks with parts (a) to (f). Candidates answer two of the three.
caption: Each question is fixed to one topic, so choose your two topics early.

alt: A table with Family and Education as rows and functionalist, Marxist and feminist as columns. Family: warm bath theory, unit of consumption, conjugal roles and domestic division of labour. Education: meritocracy and role allocation, cultural capital and the myth of meritocracy, patriarchal curriculum and gendered subject choice.
caption: Fill every cell with a specific mechanism; the table transfers straight into exam answers.
